answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, limiting how far influence can spread. A Sybil cluster with few external attestations has low conductance: only a small fraction of walk transitions cross its boundary. Min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore constrain the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, even if its members attest heavily among themselves. Labels such as pigment, orchard, and basalt do not alter that structural limit.
